[1;2m› [0mAnswer from general knowledge only. Do not use any tools, do not read any files, do not run any shell commands, do
  not browse the web. In at least 500 words of streamed prose, explain the conceptual difference between Erlang/OTP
  `:gen_statem` and `:gen_server`, covering state-enter callbacks, `:state_timeout`, and when you would reach for one
  over the other. Take your time.


[2m• [0m[38;5;6m:gen_server[39m and [38;5;6m:gen_statem[39m are both OTP behaviours for building long-running Erlang processes with structured
  callback APIs, but they model different kinds of logic.

  A [38;5;6m:gen_server[39m is best understood as a process with private data and a message-handling interface. It has one current
  “server state”, usually represented as a map, struct, tuple, or record. Incoming calls, casts, and ordinary messages
  are handled by callbacks such as [38;5;6mhandle_call/3[39m, [38;5;6mhandle_cast/2[39m, and [38;5;6mhandle_info/2[39m. Those callbacks inspect the current
  data, decide what to do, maybe reply, and return an updated data value. The shape of the callback API does not imply
  that the server is in one of several named modes. You can encode modes inside the data, of course, but OTP itself does
  not treat those modes as first-class.
